In liblmdb's `mdb.c`, the constant is defined under an `#ifndef` guard:

```c
#ifndef MDB_MAXKEYSIZE
#define MDB_MAXKEYSIZE 511
#endif
```

**Default value: 511 bytes.** That default is the documented limit ("keys are limited to 511 bytes by default").

At runtime the macro is not what gets enforced. The effective limit is held per-environment in the **`me_maxkeysize` field of `struct MDB_env`**. It is initialized from the compile-time constant when the environment is set up/opened, and:

- `mdb_env_get_maxkeysize(env)` just returns `env->me_maxkeysize`;
- `mdb_env_set_maxkeysize(env, len)` — which must be called after `mdb_env_create()` and before `mdb_env_open()` — writes the field so the limit can be changed per-environment without recompiling (in the 0.9.x stable line it can only be lowered from the default; the master branch allows raising it when the page size permits);
- key-size enforcement (the `MDB_BAD_VALSIZE` path in the put logic) compares against `env->me_maxkeysize`, not the macro.

One caveat on my offline recall: I'm confident about the value 511, the `#ifndef` guard, and the `me_maxkeysize` field with its get/set API; I have not re-derived the exact initialization line in `mdb_env_open2` verbatim.

ANSWER: MDB_MAXKEYSIZE defaults to 511 (guarded by `#ifndef MDB_MAXKEYSIZE` / `#define MDB_MAXKEYSIZE 511`); at runtime that value is copied into the per-environment field `env->me_maxkeysize` (in `struct MDB_env`) at open time, and all key-size checks use that field — it is read by `mdb_env_get_maxkeysize()` and can be overridden before open with `mdb_env_set_maxkeysize()`.
